ground_truth.modified_snippet: In Study 3, the effect of implicitly activating the analytical thinking mechanism on donation was d = 0.23, 95% CI [0.01, 0.45], regarded as a small effect.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Within-subjects impossible for learning manipulation; df in ANOVA tables inconsistent
ground_truth.original_snippet: We embedded Studies 1 and 3 of Small et al. (2007) into a single between-subject design with identifiability and intervention as the independent variables;
ground_truth.modified_snippet: We embedded Studies 1 and 3 of Small et al. (2007) into a single within-subject design with identifiability and intervention as the independent variables;
ground_truth.description: Changed between-subjects to within-subjects — impossible for this intervention (learning about IVE permanently changes cognition); df in ANOVA tables are inconsistent with within-subjects

matched_finding.description: The Design section labels the study a within-subject design, but the descriptive tables report different and non-overlapping sample sizes for each cell (e.g., 159, 175, 166), the analyses are two-way ANOVAs with a large residual df (994) consistent with between-subjects comparisons, and the original studies were between-subjects. Calling this a within-subject design is incorrect and would imply a completely different (and inappropriate) error structure for the reported tests.
matched_finding.quote: We embedded Studies 1 and 3 of Small et al. (2007) into a single within-subject design with identifiability and intervention as the independent variables

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Cognitive evaluations measured but paper discusses 'affective feelings' throughout — cross-section mismatch
ground_truth.original_snippet: After the donation, they had to fill up a questionnaire for different affective reactions they experienced which may influence their choice of donation. These items included the feeling of being upset, being touched, being sympathetic, moral responsibility, and the appropriateness of donation to hel...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: After the donation, they had to fill up a questionnaire for different cognitive evaluations they experienced which may influence their choice of donation. These items included beliefs about the severity of the crisis, the perceived trustworthiness of the charity, the expected accountability of funds...
ground_truth.description: Replaced affective measures with cognitive evaluations — IVE theory is explicitly affect-driven (affect heuristic); cognitive measures can't test the proposed emotional mechanism

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Self-selection into conditions visible but subtle — 'selected their preferred' reads naturally
ground_truth.original_snippet: Participants will be assigned randomly to the intervention and identifiability conditions.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Participants selected their preferred intervention and identifiability conditions.
ground_truth.description: Replaced random assignment with self-selection — eliminates internal validity; empathetic people may choose identifiable victim condition

matched_finding.description: The Procedures section states that participants chose their own conditions. Self-selection into experimental conditions destroys random assignment, introduces selection confounds, and makes any between-condition comparison uninterpretable as causal. This also directly contradicts the Overview, which states participants were randomly assigned. If this is literally what the Qualtrics flow does, it is a fatal design flaw; if it is a writing error it still must be corrected because it defines the core internal validity of the study.
matched_finding.quote: Participants selected their preferred intervention and identifiability conditions.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Statistical victims donate MORE contradicts the identifiable victim effect being replicated
ground_truth.original_snippet: meaning that participants who faced an identifiable victim (M=2.54, SD=1.76) tended to donate more than those who faced the statistical victims (M=2.24, SD=1.67).
ground_truth.modified_snippet: meaning that participants who faced a statistical victim (M=2.54, SD=1.76) tended to donate more than those who faced the identifiable victims (M=2.24, SD=1.67).
ground_truth.description: Reversed which condition has higher donations — IVE is now reversed (statistical > identifiable), contradicting the phenomenon being replicated and Table 11 descriptives

matched_finding.description: The post-hoc interpretation states that statistical-victim participants donated more (M=2.54) than identifiable-victim participants (M=2.24). However, the descriptive statistics in Table 7 show the identifiable condition means (2.58 and 2.50) are higher than the statistical condition means (2.46 and 2.01). The means appear swapped/mislabeled, and the verbal conclusion (statistical > identifiable) is the opposite of what the descriptive data show and the opposite of Hypothesis 1. This is a substantive inconsistency that reverses the central finding.
matched_finding.quote: participants who faced a statistical victim (M=2.54, SD=1.76) tended to donate more than those who faced the identifiable victims (M=2.24, SD=1.67).

matched_finding.subcategory: Power analysis details absent from main text
matched_finding.description: The manuscript asserts the sample was determined to ensure adequate power but provides no target effect size, alpha, power, or resulting N in the main text—only a circular statement and a pointer to supplementary material. Readers cannot evaluate whether the study is adequately powered (especially given the very small original/meta-analytic effects, e.g., d=0.23 in Study 3 and a meta-analytic mean of 0.05) without these numbers.
matched_finding.quote: The sample size for this study was determined to ensure adequate statistical power for detecting the effects reported in the original study.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Says 'no exclusion' then lists exclusions — direct contradiction
ground_truth.original_snippet: There was no exclusion of samples in this study.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Participants who indicated they had prior knowledge of the identifiable victim effect were excluded, as well as those who failed the attention check.
ground_truth.description: Added non-preregistered exclusions — prior-knowledge exclusion biases toward IVE-naive participants; contradicts 'no exclusion' claim earlier

matched_finding.description: Participants with prior knowledge of the effect and those failing the attention check are said to be excluded, but no counts are given and analyses appear to use the full N=1000. The number excluded, the resulting analyzed N per cell, and whether exclusions differ across conditions are needed to evaluate bias and to reproduce the analyses.
matched_finding.quote: Participants who indicated they had prior knowledge of the identifiable victim effect were excluded, as well as those who failed the attention check.

The "availability heuristic"  (Tversky & Kahneman, 1973), which relies on the ease of retrieving relevant instances from memory, is believed to be activated whe...
ground_truth.description: Replaced affect heuristic (emotional arousal) with availability heuristic (memory retrieval) — changes the theoretical mechanism; intervention design and feeling measures no longer match the theory

matched_finding.subcategory: Availability heuristic vs. affect heuristic conflation
matched_finding.description: The introduction attributes the affective response to identifiable victims to the 'availability heuristic,' but the mechanism described (stronger affect/sympathy driving valuation) corresponds to the affect heuristic emphasized by Slovic and by Small & Loewenstein, and reflected in the keyword 'affective heuristics.' Misattributing the mechanism to availability (ease of retrieval from memory) reflects a conceptual mislabeling of the theoretical framework.
matched_finding.quote: The “availability heuristic”  (Tversky & Kahneman, 1973), which relies on the ease of retrieving relevant instances from memory, is believed to be activated when we value a personalized individual
